analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/developer/test.md (lines 2692-3152 and 3153-3501+). Only the head side of the file was supplied. I reviewed it as documentation of benchmark and test procedures, and no code or configuration change is visible.

Security-relevant content touched on:
- Prefix-cache and SSD KV benchmarking (T-041, TB-007). The doc describes test-only isolation env vars: DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL, _TEST_ROOT and _TEST_PERSISTENT_KEY. It also describes the persistent-test-namespace and access-group seam.
- That seam is stated to reject ephemeral fallback for a namespace, to refuse unsafe roots, to keep key bytes in the Secure Enclave/Keychain, and to export no key bytes.
- The text says the test root override is ignored without the affirmative isolation opt-in. This is consistent with the T-041 mitigations on storage validation and KEK-rooted HMAC names, and nothing contradicts the 30-minute TTL or the default-on posture.
- The cache-key and namespace controls are test-only and documented as not isolating full HTTP provider attestation. Whether the implementing code actually enforces these gates cannot be checked from this PR. The code was not supplied, so this is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
- Docs describe a benchmark attention-packet capture that writes native tensor bytes. These are diagnostic benchmark outputs, not production paths.
- A CI doc change mentions a signed-commit verification job. This is not a runtime security boundary.

No visible change to TB-001 to TB-011 trust assumptions, to App Attest authorization (T-052 to T-058), or to authorization, encryption, billing or availability paths. The threat model needs no update from these units.

For the next pass: if other files in this PR change the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_* env handling, SSDPrefixCachePolicy, or persistent test key loaders, check that the doc claims (override ignored without opt-in, no ephemeral fallback for a namespace) match the code.
